handback.t:
CAP-1 done. One new bin, `src/bin/f1_lab.rs` (std plus existing rayon and serde_json). I did not touch the library, spawn agents, commit or download anything. The full run takes about 16 s and re-runs byte-identical apart from `runtime_s`.

**Rerun** (set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-hr`):
- `cargo run --offline --release --bin f1_lab -- --out results/f1_lab.json`
- `cargo run --offline --release --bin f1_lab -- --held 61-90 --out results/f1_lab_confirm61-90.json`
- `cargo run --offline --release --bin f1_lab -- --exp a1 --np 300 --out results/f1_a1_np300.json`

**Protocol**
- Tuned on seeds 1-8, held-out 31-60, frozen confirmation 61-90.
- Paired 95% t-CI against the best per cell of {keyword, eps-greedy, pooled-ts, hebbian-robust, warm(hebr), guarded(hebr)}.
- Holm correction per experiment and globally. Every experiment includes control cells.
- Control cells were excluded from tuning. I relabelled A1's correct8 world as a control after seeing that tuning on it picked a do-nothing config.

**Results.** None meets the unconditional bar of beating the best fair baseline in more than one world.

- **A1, warm transfer (child router inherits a parent's learned feature-to-agent map): conditional win.**
  - It wins in traps8 and many16 when the child resembles the parent. Traps8 with no change: +0.121 at H100 (the first 100 tasks), falling to +0.027 at H2000. Many16: +0.064 to +0.017. The confirmation set agrees (traps8 +0.097 to +0.025, many16 +0.065 to +0.018).
  - A child with transfer averages 0.796 success over its first 100 tasks. The best baseline averages 0.786 over its first 2000.
  - The parent's own 1000 training tasks are not counted, so this saves work across deployments but is not free.
  - It loses when the child is unrelated (-0.03 to -0.135) and in correct8, where the keyword prior is already near-optimal (-0.013 up to -0.145). At half the topics changed, many16 loses up to -0.044.
  - Copying the parent's full state is dominated. Nothing detects relatedness for free, so this is opt-in only, and only when you know the child is related.
- **A2, new agent added mid-run (inherits a declared sibling's evidence):** wins in 1 of 2 worlds. Correct8 with an upgraded sibling gains about +0.009 to +0.013, Holm-significant in both sets. The same upgrade in traps8 is not significant. The inheritance step adds only about +0.002 over the cold version of the same mechanism, so most of the gain comes from the slot-sharing, not from inheriting evidence. A wrongly declared sibling loses about -0.017. Not a win by the bar.
- **B, task ordering / curriculum for a reorderable queue: negative.** There are no Holm wins or losses outside the control worlds, and the effect against first-in-first-out ordering is about +0.001. Order doesn't change the per-topic learning cost with independent topics.
- **C, multi-objective routing (quality, cost, latency):**
  - Pooling evidence across tenants with different preference weights wins: +0.037 (traps8) and +0.028 (many16) across 4 tenants, +0.10 and +0.078 for a new tenant with an unseen preference joining at t=1000. The confirmation set agrees.
  - The gain is from pooling evidence that per-tenant scalarized rewards can't share. Shared minus separate decoupled learners is +0.084/+0.067 for the new tenant and +0.033/+0.019 across 4 tenants. A single tenant ties or loses slightly (traps8 -0.008).
  - A mid-run preference switch gives no benefit (+0.001, not significant).
  - The learned quality/cost/latency frontier recovers 0.91 to 0.97 of the true hypervolume (traps8). The keyword prior alone already gives 0.91 to 0.95.
- **D, router-committee disagreement as a difficulty signal:**
  - It is a useful signal: AUC 0.71-0.83 for predicting a bad committee choice, against 0.54-0.63 for low evidence alone.
  - It does not convert into a routing gain. Plurality is +0.0066 in traps8 (not significant) and -0.009 in the correct8 control. Disagreement-gated exploration is the same as plain plurality, and the learned-weight vote is worse.

**Global Holm** over 425 tests: 63 wins and 143 losses on 31-60, 61 and 128 on 61-90. The losses are almost all the control cells.

**Caveats**
- Worlds are my own generators, not real traffic.
- I looked at 31-60 during development. My first A2 attempt lost badly against the best baseline, so I switched its base router after that run. 61-90 was never examined before the final runs.
- Cargo tests were not rerun, since the library is unchanged. The bin builds without warnings.

The results block is appended to `results/research_board.md`, starting "### VERIFY REQUEST — CAP-1 — f1 sample-efficiency mechanisms".
